source.title: Does Continual Learning = Catastrophic Forgetting?
source.authors: A. Thai; Stefan Stojanov; Isaac Rehg; James M. Rehg

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies continual learning and forgetting, not whether independently trained models converge in representation as model scale or capability increases. Its representation analyses compare continually trained classifiers with a batch-trained model, which does not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: Section G measures representation similarity to a batch model using CKA and a visual-feature classifier. The authors relate this to forgetting in continual classification, not to convergence across independently trained models, scale, modalities, or interchangeability. The highlighted results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: A continual-learning study of forgetting and knowledge transfer in 3D shape reconstruction and classification. Its only representation-similarity analysis (Supp. G) compares continually trained classifiers against a batch-trained oracle model on the same data. That tracks forgetting over learning exposures, not convergence across independently trained models, scale, modalities, seeds, mapping or universal features. No version is tested. The record's relation 'tests' contradicts its own T6 tranche; it should be 'cites_only' (CKA is cited as a tool).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The main conclusion is that continual 3D shape and 2.5D/2D reconstruction tasks show no catastrophic forgetting and show positive forward and backward transfer under vanilla SGD. The authors also find that smaller output-distribution shift goes with better transfer, and that shape reconstruction can serve as a proxy task for continual classification. The representation-versus-accuracy finding is a supplementary point, not a headline conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: No method from the original sources is tested; this is a continual-learning study.

fits_no_version.finding: Continually trained classifiers' penultimate features stay much closer to a batch-trained model (CKA, VF probe, fine-tuned FC) than class-output accuracy suggests. YASS with 500 exemplars is more batch-similar than iCaRL with 2000, yet less accurate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In class-incremental learning, feature-representation similarity to a batch model degrades less than output accuracy, and the two can rank methods differently.

record.problems: The representation-analysis results are presented as plots without exact numerical values or uncertainty estimates. They compare continual classifiers with a batch model and do not assess scale or cross-modal convergence.
record.rows_left_out: Other plotted configurations and methods in Fig. 18 are not separately extracted; the text does not state their individual outcomes, and the representation analyses do not test a listed claim version.

untested.parts: all; no comparison across random seeds of the same architecture
all; the VF probe trains a linear readout of batch features but is used only to measure forgetting

record.verdict_notes: Off-topic for representation convergence. It is retained only because it uses CKA. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Scale- and capability-related convergence across independently trained models.
Cross-modal alignment of vision and language models on paired images and captions.
Convergence across random initializations of the same architecture.
Mapping, stitching, or otherwise transferring representations between models.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Dependence of convergence on similarity metrics, settings, or input data.
Whether representation alignment is incomplete or explained by shared training data or objectives.

rows.subject: YASS
rows.operation_detail: Compared the classifier's feature representation at learning exposures with the batch model's representation using CKA.
rows.note: The plotted result is reported across learning exposures. The text says this representation analysis shows less forgetting than class-output accuracy, but gives no exact CKA values.
rows.check: CKA to a batch model of the same lineage measures forgetting, not cross-model convergence. The value is figure-only.

rows.subject: iCaRL
rows.operation_detail: Compared the classifier's feature representation at learning exposures with the batch model's representation using CKA.
rows.note: The text explicitly compares this curve with YASS using 500 exemplars and says the latter's representation is more similar to the batch model.
rows.check: Same as R1. The subject is iCaRL with 2000 exemplars, the green curve the text contrasts with YASS-500.

rows.subject: YASS
rows.operation_detail: Trained visual-feature classifiers on the model's representation to predict binarized batch-model features.
rows.baseline: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet34 is described as a lower bound
rows.note: This analysis evaluates how well the representation captures information related to the batch representation; the text gives no exact accuracy values.
rows.check: VF-classifier accuracy against binarized batch features is a forgetting probe, not a convergence measure. The value is figure-only. The 'numbers_found 1/1' entry seems to refer to the threshold θ=1, which is not a result.
